_about: Set 25 — the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework. Written from scratch after a candidate reported the live CLF-C02 exam leaning harder on CAF than the community question bank does. Same format as set 24: a rationale under every option and one line naming the idea under test. Not copied from AWS or any paid question bank.

questions.q: An organisation is planning a cloud programme and wants a structure for identifying capability gaps across the whole business, not just in engineering. Which AWS framework is designed for this?
o: The Six Advantages of Cloud Computing
questions.k: CAF looks at the organisation; Well-Architected looks at a workload. The word to catch is who or what is being assessed.

r.A: Well-Architected reviews a single workload's design against six pillars. It has nothing to say about staffing or governance.
r.B: Correct. CAF exists to find capability gaps across business, people, governance, platform, security and operations.
r.C: The shared responsibility model divides security duties between AWS and the customer. It is not a planning framework.
r.D: The six advantages are a sales argument for the cloud, not a method for assessing readiness.

questions.q: How many perspectives make up the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework, and what are they?
o: Four: people, process, technology and cost
Five: envision, align, launch, scale and optimise
Six: business, people, governance, platform, security and operations
Six: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimisation and sustainability
questions.k: Six perspectives. Note that the other six-item list belongs to Well-Architected, which is the classic trap on this question.

r.A: People, process and technology is a generic consulting model, not CAF.
r.B: Envision, align, launch and scale are the four CAF transformation phases, not the perspectives — and there are four, not five.
r.C: Correct. Business, people and governance cover the organisation; platform, security and operations cover the technology.
r.D: That list is the six Well-Architected pillars. Different framework, different purpose.

questions.q: A CFO wants assurance that the cloud programme will produce a measurable return and that IT spending will map to business outcomes. Which CAF perspective covers this concern?
questions.k: The business perspective is about making sure cloud investment produces business results — the stakeholders are the CFO, CIO and business unit leaders.

r.A: Correct. Aligning IT strategy and investment with measurable business outcomes is exactly what this perspective covers.
r.B: Governance is about managing and measuring the programme itself — portfolio, risk, benefits realisation — rather than justifying the investment.
r.C: Platform covers the architecture and the technical estate. It answers how, not why.
r.D: Operations covers running services to the level the business agreed. It comes after the case is made.

questions.q: During a CAF assessment, a company finds that its staff lack cloud skills and that roles and incentives still assume an on-premises operating model. Which perspective addresses this?
questions.k: The people perspective is the bridge between technology and business: culture, skills, roles, org structure and change management.

r.A: The business perspective is about outcomes and investment, not about who does the work.
r.B: Correct. Training, role design, culture and change management all sit under the people perspective.
r.C: Governance would track whether the skills programme delivers, but it does not design it.
r.D: Security covers protecting data and workloads, not workforce readiness.

questions.q: A programme office needs to manage the migration portfolio, track benefits and keep cloud risk visible to the board. Which CAF perspective is this?
questions.k: Governance is about orchestrating the initiative and measuring it — portfolio management, benefits, risk, data curation and programme control.

r.A: Operations keeps live services running to their agreed levels. It is day-to-day, not programme-level.
r.B: Platform is about the technical architecture and the environments themselves.
r.C: Correct. Portfolio management, benefits realisation and risk management sit squarely in the governance perspective.
r.D: People handles skills and culture, not portfolio and risk tracking.

questions.q: An enterprise architect is defining the target architecture, the landing zone and the pattern for building new workloads on AWS. Which CAF perspective covers this work?
questions.k: Platform is the engineering perspective — the CTO, architects and engineers building the target environment and the products that run in it.

r.A: Correct. Target architecture, platform engineering and modernisation all belong to the platform perspective.
r.B: Operations takes over once workloads are live: monitoring, incidents, events and problems.
r.C: The business perspective would justify the investment, not design the landing zone.
r.D: Governance would set the standards the architecture must satisfy, but not draw it.

questions.q: A team is defining how incidents will be detected, escalated and resolved once workloads are live in AWS, and how service levels will be met. Which CAF perspective is this?
questions.k: The operations perspective covers running and supporting cloud services to the level the business agreed — observability, incidents, problems and change.

r.A: Platform builds the environment. Keeping it healthy afterwards is a different perspective.
r.B: Security covers threats and compliance, not general service delivery.
r.C: Governance measures the programme; it does not run the service desk.
r.D: Correct. Event, incident and problem management, and meeting agreed service levels, are the operations perspective.

questions.q: Which capabilities belong to the security perspective of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework? (Choose two.)
o: Benefits realisation of the cloud programme
Choosing which instance families to standardise on
questions.k: The security perspective covers confidentiality, integrity and availability: governance of security, identity, threat detection, vulnerability management, infrastructure and data protection, and incident response.

r.A: Correct. Identity and access management is one of the named security perspective capabilities.
r.B: Benefits realisation belongs to the governance perspective.
r.C: Correct. Threat detection and incident response are both security perspective capabilities.
r.D: Skills training is the people perspective.
r.E: Standardising instance families is a platform decision.

questions.q: AWS CAF describes four transformation phases. Which sequence is correct?
questions.k: Envision the outcomes, align the stakeholders, launch pilots, then scale what works. Do not confuse these with the migration strategies or with the MAP phases.

r.A: Assess, mobilise, migrate and modernise are the phases of the Migration Acceleration Program, a different thing.
r.B: Correct. Envision, align, launch, scale is the CAF transformation journey.
r.C: Plan, build, run is generic IT lifecycle language, not CAF.
r.D: Those are migration strategies — part of the 7 Rs — not transformation phases.

questions.q: In which CAF transformation phase does an organisation identify and prioritise the business outcomes it expects the cloud to deliver?
questions.k: Envision comes first and is about outcomes, not technology: what should be different for the business once this is done?

r.A: Correct. Envision identifies and prioritises the transformation opportunities tied to business outcomes.
r.B: Align comes next and is about finding capability gaps and building stakeholder agreement.
r.C: Launch is about delivering pilots in production to demonstrate value.
r.D: Scale expands what the pilots proved, to the level of demand.

questions.q: A company has run two successful production pilots on AWS and now wants to expand them to full business scale while sustaining the benefits. Which CAF phase describes this?
questions.k: Launch proves value in production on a small scale; scale expands that to the level the business needs and keeps the benefits going.

r.A: Envision happens before anything is built.
r.B: Align is where capability gaps and stakeholder concerns are worked through, well before pilots run.
r.C: Launch is the pilot stage itself, which this company has already completed.
r.D: Correct. Expanding proven pilots to full scale and sustaining the benefits is the scale phase.

questions.q: What is the difference between the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework and the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
o: CAF assesses an organisation's readiness to adopt cloud; Well-Architected reviews a workload's design
CAF applies to migrations; Well-Architected applies to new builds
CAF is for enterprises; Well-Architected is for start-ups
CAF is a paid engagement; Well-Architected is free
questions.k: The unit of analysis is the giveaway. CAF assesses an organisation; Well-Architected assesses a workload.

r.A: Correct. One looks at capability across the business, the other at how a specific workload is designed and run.
r.B: Well-Architected applies to any workload, migrated or newly built.
r.C: Neither framework is restricted by company size.
r.D: Both are free to use. The Well-Architected Tool is in the console, and CAF is published guidance.

questions.q: Which three CAF perspectives are most concerned with the organisation rather than the technology?
questions.k: CAF splits neatly in half: business, people and governance are organisational; platform, security and operations are technical.

r.A: Those three are the technical half of CAF.
r.B: Correct. Business, people and governance address strategy, culture and control rather than systems.
r.C: Those are transformation phases, not perspectives.
r.D: Those are Well-Architected pillars.

questions.q: AWS CAF names several transformation domains that the perspectives support. Which of the following is one of them?
questions.k: The four transformation domains are technology, process, organisation and people. Anything else on the list is invented.

r.A: Finance shows up inside the business perspective, but it is not one of the transformation domains.
r.B: Correct. Organisational transformation is one of the four, alongside technology, process and people.
r.C: Regulation is handled through governance and security, not as its own domain.
r.D: Vendor management is a governance activity, not a transformation domain.

questions.q: A retailer is reorganising from project teams into product teams so that each team owns a service end to end. Which CAF transformation domain does this represent?
questions.k: Organisational transformation is about how teams are arranged around business outcomes; people transformation is about the culture and skills of the individuals in them.

r.A: Technology transformation covers migrating and modernising the estate itself.
r.B: Process transformation is about digitising and optimising how work flows.
r.C: Correct. Restructuring teams around products and outcomes is organisational transformation.
r.D: People transformation would cover the training and culture change that accompanies it, not the restructure.

questions.q: Which statement about the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework is TRUE?
o: It is available only to customers on Enterprise Support
It certifies that a workload meets a compliance standard
It is free published guidance any organisation can apply
It replaces the need for a migration business case
questions.k: CAF is guidance, not a product, a certification or a paywalled service. Anyone can read it and run the assessment themselves.

r.A: There is no support plan requirement. AWS Professional Services can help, but the framework itself is open.
r.B: Compliance certification comes from audits, and the evidence from AWS Artifact. CAF certifies nothing.
r.C: Correct. It is published guidance, free to use, with AWS or a partner optionally facilitating the assessment.
r.D: A business case is still needed. CAF helps you build one rather than removing it.

questions.q: During the align phase of a CAF engagement, what is the main activity?
o: Running the first production workloads to prove value
Identifying capability gaps and building stakeholder agreement
Expanding proven workloads across the organisation
Choosing which AWS Region to deploy into
questions.k: Align is where the gaps between where you are and where you want to be get named, and where the people who must agree are brought together.

r.A: Running the first production workloads is the launch phase.
r.B: Correct. Align surfaces capability gaps, dependencies and stakeholder concerns, producing an action plan.
r.C: Expanding what worked is the scale phase.
r.D: Region selection is a delivery decision, not a CAF phase activity.

questions.q: Which CAF perspective would help a company decide how to fund cloud spending and manage it as an operating expense rather than a capital purchase?
questions.k: Cloud financial management sits under the business perspective, because it is about how the organisation funds and measures technology investment.

r.A: Correct. Cloud financial management is one of the business perspective's named capabilities.
r.B: Platform is concerned with architecture, not with how the bill is funded.
r.C: Operations runs the services; it does not decide the funding model.
r.D: Security has no role in how spend is classified.

questions.q: A company wants AWS specialists working alongside its own staff to run a CAF assessment and shape the roadmap. Which AWS offering provides this?
questions.k: CAF is free to read, but running the assessment with AWS people is a paid engagement through Professional Services, or through an APN partner.

r.A: Trusted Advisor is an automated checking tool. It cannot facilitate a workshop.
r.B: Correct. Professional Services is the AWS consulting arm that runs engagements alongside customer teams.
r.C: Artifact provides compliance reports and nothing else.
r.D: Basic Support offers no technical or advisory engagement at all.

questions.q: Which pair correctly matches a CAF perspective to one of its capabilities?
questions.k: Data curation, risk management, portfolio management and benefits realisation all sit under governance — the perspective that measures and controls the programme.

r.A: Vulnerability management is a security perspective capability.
r.B: Correct. Data curation is one of the governance perspective's named capabilities.
r.C: Cloud financial management belongs to the business perspective.
r.D: Organisational alignment belongs to the people perspective.
